title: What Rainier Paws' customers are saying

0.label: Booking app double books
0.summary: Since the spring app update, customers report double bookings, appointments cancelled or moved on their own, and even no-show fees charged for app-cancelled visits.
0.action: Roll back or fix the app update, refund every no-show fee charged on an app-cancelled booking, and offer phone booking until it is stable.

1.label: Daycare tires dogs out
1.summary: Owners love that daycare sends their high-energy or anxious dogs home happy, calm and exhausted, and they appreciate staff knowing each dog and texting updates.
1.action: Feature these quotes on the website and offer a two-days-a-week daycare package for high-energy breeds.

2.label: Everyone loves Kenji
2.summary: Kenji is praised as a meticulous, patient groomer whose clients follow him, though he is so popular that his slots are hard to get.
2.action: Prompt Kenji's clients to prebook their next groom at checkout, and have Kenji mentor other groomers on scissor work.

3.label: Pickups run hours late
3.summary: Dogs are ready hours after the quoted time, with some crated all day waiting their turn and owners stuck at the counter or in their cars.
3.action: Quote pickup windows based on the actual day's schedule, and text owners as soon as a delay becomes clear rather than at the end.

4.label: Surprise fees and price hikes
4.summary: Customers are upset by de-matting and other add-on fees that appear only at pickup and by repeated price increases; the group also includes one thank-you for a donated charity groom.
4.action: Call before adding any fee over the quote, and make the website prices match what the counter charges.

5.label: Kennel cough outbreak
5.summary: A kennel cough outbreak spread through daycare and many owners heard about it secondhand, though several praise the stricter vaccine rule that followed.
5.action: Write a simple plan for emailing all daycare families the same day any illness is spotted, and keep the vaccine requirement.

6.label: Daycare webcam keeps breaking
6.summary: The daycare live cam is a major reason people choose and pay for daycare, but it is frozen or offline for days or weeks at a time.
6.action: Replace or repair the camera setup this month and post a status update whenever it goes down.

7.label: Doodles shaved, not teddy
7.summary: Owners who asked for a fluffy teddy bear cut got their doodles shaved, often with no phone call first; one owner says a printed photo with written lengths finally got it right.
7.action: Require a call before any shave-down and use a written cut card with a photo and blade length for every doodle groom.

8.label: Gentle with nervous dogs
8.summary: Owners are moved by the patient handling of fearful, anxious and elderly dogs, though a couple of reports describe bleeding nicks that nobody mentioned at pickup.
8.action: Offer the 'happy visit' intro as a named service, and make telling the owner about any nick at pickup a firm rule.

9.label: Brooke's cuts hit or miss
9.summary: Brooke is kind and improving, but her scissor work on faces and feet is uneven and some clients ask for Kenji instead.
9.action: Pair Brooke with Kenji for scissor-finish practice and give her longer slots so she isn't rushed.

10.label: People want cat grooming
10.summary: Cat owners are asking for grooming and nail trims, and they are confused because the website says 'pet grooming' and the app lets them book a cat.
10.action: Remove 'cat' from the app and change the website to say 'dog grooming', or test cat nail trims if demand looks strong.

11.label: Cramped shared parking lot
11.summary: The small lot shared with the laundromat is chaotic at morning dropoff and the tow signs confuse people; the group also includes one unrelated happy family review.
11.action: Ask the laundromat about reserving a few spots for dropoff, and tell new clients where to park on the side street.

12.label: Walk-in nail trims
12.summary: The cheap, fast walk-in nail trims are a favorite, but people are frustrated by no weekend hours, no tap to pay, and a 'walk-ins welcome' sign that isn't always true.
12.action: Post the actual walk-in hours on the sign and online, and add tap to pay at the counter.

13.label: Treats and retail shelf
13.summary: Customers love the local treats and paw balm but say the shelf is small and the popular items are often sold out; one former customer asks about shipping.
13.action: Keep the best sellers like the salmon jerky, freeze-dried chicken and dental chews stocked, and consider simple online orders for customers who have moved away.

14.label: Clipper burn and nicks
14.summary: Several dogs came home with clipper burn, rashes, or small cuts near the eyelid and lip, and some needed vet care.
14.action: Check blade temperature and use longer blades on bellies and sanitary areas, and follow up with a call after any skin issue.

15.label: Photo events and good vibes
15.summary: This group mixes praise for the Halloween and holiday charity photo events with general comments about the clean shop and cute Instagram, plus one lukewarm review.
15.action: Plan the next holiday photo charity event and promote it on Instagram.
